title: Callisto Telecom outreach scratchpad
content:
Quick notes + plan for outreach to Callisto Telecom (regional carrier, retail + SMB vertical). Goal = pilot for call-center LLM assist + network incident summarization. Keep initial ask lightweight: 6-week pilot, 1 dedicated GPU node or hosted trial with strict data retention/ephemeral logs.

Background signals:
- Recent press: acquired LocalMesh (edge cell management) — likely interest in transforming ops with LLMs.
- Hiring: Sr. Customer Ops role posted; indicates focus on contact center efficiency.
- Public docs: internal tooling stacks on Kafka + K8s; some on-prem footprints for legacy BSS/OSS.

Decision-makers (surface-level):
- CTO: Arjun Mehta (platform + infra) — cares about latency/ops cost.
- Head of Customer Ops: Sophie Tran — owner for contact center pilots.
- Security/compliance: Dir. InfoSec: Omar Karim — will want KMS/HSM + audit guarantees.
- Procurement: VP Biz Ops: Claire Duval.

Why Redwood is a fit (thesis hooks):
- Predictable latency and routing: can run private or dedicated with regional routing to keep RTT low for live agent assist.
- Data isolation + KMS integrations: addresses InfoSec concerns for CPE data and call logs.
- Cost controls (batching/caching): helps keep per-minute transcription+generation costs predictable for large volume contact centers.
- Rollouts & fallbacks: can degrade to smaller model variant during peak traffic without disrupting agent workflows.

Pilot proposal (6 weeks):
1) Scope: live agent assist (real-time suggestions) + nightly incident-summary pipeline for NOC.
2) Metrics: average agent handle time reduction target (10–15%), summary recall/precision for incident triage >80% in rubric.
3) Infra: dedicated single-GPU node in region or Private VPC deployment; retention window 7 days default, optional S3 auto-archive.
4) Security: KMS integration, audit log stream to their SIEM (placeholder: Splunk), SOC2 addendum.
5) Commercial: pilot credit + engineering time cap (40h) from Redwood; after pilot convert to committed Dedicated or Hosted with egress billing.

Outbound messaging (short, 2 variations):
- Email A (intro): "Arjun — curious if Callisto is exploring LLMs for contact center and NOC automation? We helped a regional carrier cut AHT by 12% while preserving call quality; short pilot could prove model ops and security fit. Can we do a 20-minute intro next week?"
- Email B (security-first): "Omar — heard you lead InfoSec for Callisto. Quick note: Redwood supports customer-managed KMS, private VPCs, and audit streams; we run private inference for regulated carriers. Happy to share a short design doc and SOC2 details if useful."

LinkedIn/DM script (very short):
- "Hi Sophie — Maya from Redwood. We run pilots for telco contact centers (agent assist + incident summaries). 15-min chat to see if this is useful?"

Discovery questions to ask on first call:
- Current contact center platform? (Genesys, Avaya, NICE, homegrown?)
- Volume: peak TPS and avg call length, % calls routed to live agents.
- Where are call logs/transcripts currently stored? retention policy?
- Existing SOC/Compliance constraints (data residency, access controls, encryption).
- Nightly NOC workflows: what is manual today? painpoints?
- Primary success metrics for a pilot (ops savings, NPS, MTTR).

Anticipated objections + short counters:
- "We can't send call audio to a 3rd party": propose Private deployment or Dedicated in their VPC + KMS, and ephemeral cache; show audit logs + can run air-gapped proof-of-concept in our Private bundle.
- "Models hallucinate on incident data": recommend prompt templates, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with strong source attribution, and metricized quality gating; include calibration phase in pilot.
- "Cost too high for scale": pitch batching + KV-caching for repetitive dialogs; show cost model with break-even at X calls/day (prepare spreadsheet).
- "Integration complexity with legacy OSS/BSS": propose phased approach: ingest nightly dumps for NOC summaries first (low risk), then real-time via adapter layer. Redwood prebuilt connectors reduce integration time.

Open questions / things to prep: (TODOs)
- Get anonymized call volume numbers (Sophie) — action: Liam to ask in intro email. due: 2026-03-10
- Prepare 1-pager security design (KMS + audit + network flow) — owner: Maya. due: 2026-03-08
- Create cost example spreadsheet for 3 scale scenarios (10k, 50k, 200k calls/day) — owner: Renee. due: 2026-03-12
- Draft SOW template for 6-week pilot with 40 engineering hours cap — owner: Maya + Legal review. due: 2026-03-15

Meeting prep checklist (short):
- Slide deck: 6 slides (Problem, Redwood intro, pilot scope, security, metrics & timeline, next steps). keep visuals lightweight.
- Bring sample transcripts + redaction plan.
- Bring SOC2 summary + KMS diagram.

Notes-to-self (brainstorm):
- Might be an opportunity to bundle with our Dedicated edge offering near their LocalMesh acquisition — pitching as co-innovation with minimal infra change.
- Consider offering sequencing: NOC summaries -> agent assist -> proactive churn detection via QA.

Recent outreach history: none yet. Plan: cold intro to Arjun (CTO) + Sophie (Head Customer Ops) cc Omar (InfoSec) — short tailored email, follow up with security-first note to Omar. If no response in 7 days, try LinkedIn to Sophie.

End-of-file quick checklist:
- Add cited case study of "regional carrier" (anonymized) to 1-pager.
- Confirm legal template for pilot credits.

-- Maya

(Loose/working notes; will refine after first calls)
